Q: Can I stop hidden VBA UserForms from showing up in the preview from the Windows Taskbar? A:

Thank you @Tim Williams for the suggestion, it's enabled me to solve the problem, and here is how in case anyone else needs in future. Bare bones from this post: https://www.mrexcel.com/board/threads/userform-startup-position.671108/

I've made the following 2 functions: one to move a UserForm offscreen when it is cancelled (or continue button is clicked); one to move a UserForm to the centre of the screen when it is activated.

Public Sub U_FormToCentre(ByRef Form As Object)
' Purpose:
'   Centre the UserForm in the application window.
' Parameters:
'   Form: The UserForm to be centred.

Dim AppXCenter As Long
Dim AppYCenter As Long

AppXCenter = Application.Left + (Application.Width / 2)
AppYCenter = Application.Top + (Application.Height / 2)
With Form
    .StartUpPosition = 0
    .Top = AppYCenter - (Form.Height / 2)
    .Left = AppXCenter - (Form.Width / 2)
End With

End Sub


Public Sub U_FormOffScreen(ByRef Form As Object)
' Purpose:
'   Move the UserForm so it does not overlay the application window.
' Parameters:
'   Form: The UserForm to be moved.

Dim YTarget As Long

YTarget = Application.Top - 1000
With Form
    .StartUpPosition = 0
    .Top = YTarget
End With

End Sub

Then the bare bones of code for any UserForm is:

Option Explicit

Private Cancelled                       As Boolean

Public Property Get IsCancelled() As Boolean
IsCancelled = Cancelled
End Property

Private Sub CommandButton1_Click()
U_FormOffScreen Me
Me.Hide
End Sub

Private Sub UserForm_QueryClose(Cancel As Integer, CloseMode As Integer)
If CloseMode = VbQueryClose.vbFormControlMenu Then
    Cancel = True
    OnCancel
End If
End Sub

Private Sub OnCancel()
    Cancelled = True
    U_FormOffScreen Me
    Hide
End Sub

Private Sub UserForm_Activate()
Cancelled = False
U_FormToCentre Me
End Sub

Then a sub that runs the UserForm:

Option Explicit

Private UserForm1Demo As UserForm1

Sub DemonstrateUserForm1()

If UserForm1Demo Is Nothing Then Set UserForm1Demo = New UserForm1
UserForm1Demo.Show
    
End Sub

Q: Converting Text URLs to Clickable Hyperlinks in Excel with VBA A:

An easy way to add links is to use the HYPERLINK worksheet function. Added benefit: when you need to change a link you simply edit the text in the (adjacent) cell the HYPERLINK cell points to. Example: Suppose the link is in cell A1:

    =HYPERLINK(A1,"Link text goes here, if omitted displays the link itself")
